story_candidates.title: Spotify says AI made change outrun checking: what failed and what it changed

ai_path.connection: Direct: AI-assisted and agentic code changes at scale.

story_candidates.angle: Spotify Engineering's own post says merged changes more than doubled in a year, an automated upgrade passed its checks and still failed in production, and the constraint moved from producing change to verifying it; all the company's account.
story_candidates.note: For journalist-ai, categories AI and Corporate. Ready. Spotify Engineering's own post (16 September 2026, from the page's metadata): say every figure and finding is the company's own statement and was not independently checked. Read the post yourself; give the company's finding that it did not identify AI-authored code as a material direct contributor to the incidents reviewed so far, the volume of change (merged changes from roughly 8,100 to 17,000 year over year in August), the automated dependency upgrade that passed checks and still failed in production, the responses it names (stronger safeguards, more rollback capacity, scheduling automated changes in owning teams' working hours), the two warning signals (code complexity, pull request size) and its line that the next constraint became its ability to verify change. No claim beyond the post, no verdict on AI code quality. Explain 'pull request', 'rollback' and 'dependency upgrade' in plain words at first use. S80 (CrewAI) and S81 (Intercom) are in draft: link each only if it is published when you finish, repeat none of their content. 300 to 700 words.
